note: Rimonabant reached PWS adults in 2007 on adult-obesity data with no PWS model; the Magel2-null mouse was first used for the class in 2016 (JD5037) and nothing tested in it has reached patients, while the cannabidiol trials (2018–22) ran without PWS-model data and were terminated for sponsor reasons at n=7 and n=4.
label: Prader-Willi (CB1)

engagement.note: Patient plasma 2-AG was raised but the mice showed it only in hypothalamus; no CB1 drug has been dosed to PWS patients with engagement measured.
engagement.quote: In contrast to the abnormal circulating eCB levels in subjects with PWS, we could not discern any major changes in eCB ‘tone’ in the serum, brain, and fat pads of Magel2-null mice.
engagement.reason: No engagement readout in PWS patients
engagement.judgement: Knani 2016 (full text read) is the only paper that puts PWS patients and a PWS model side by side for this target: plasma 2-AG and arachidonic acid were raised in two patient cohorts, whereas Magel2-null mice showed no change in serum, whole brain or fat and a rise only in hypothalamic 2-AG/AA. That is a target-biology comparison, not drug engagement, and it is partly discordant; no CB1 ligand has been given to PWS patients with any occupancy or biomarker readout (rimonabant, NCT00603109, measured weight, DEXA fat, ghrelin, leptin, IGF-1 only), so the status is untested. magnitude/source_calls_it left null because no drug was compared.

dose.note: JD5037 3 mg/kg/d i.p. for 28 days normalised weight and intake; no peripheral CB1 antagonist has been dosed in PWS.
dose.short: Mouse dose never carried to patients
dose.quote: To further augment their obese phenotype, we fed both genotypes with a HFD for 12 weeks, then began daily treatment with JD5037 (3 mg/kg/d, i.p.) for 28 days.
dose.reason: No patient exposure for any model-tested drug
dose.judgement: The only exposure target the model produced (JD5037 or SLV319 3 mg/kg/d i.p., brain/plasma ratio <2%) was never carried into a PWS trial: a registry search for JD5037/CRB-4001, nimacimab, TM38837, INV-202/monlunabant, ibipinabant, taranabant and otenabant in PWS returned nothing (2026-11-02). Rimonabant's 20 mg/d (NCT00603109) and cannabidiol's 10-40 mg/kg/d (NCT02844933, NCT05098509) were set before any PWS model had been dosed with those drugs, so neither tests a model prediction.

efficacy.note: JD5037 reversed hyperphagia and obesity in the mice; the only patient test, rimonabant (n=10, 2007–09), predates the model and gave a non-significant trend.
efficacy.short: Mouse CB1 blockade; patient data a trend
efficacy.quote: Since the globally acting CBR antagonist rimonabant reduced body weight and improved metabolic features in humans with PWS, we compared the effect of JD5037 to its brain-penetrant parent compound, SLV319.
efficacy.judgement: This is the one real call. Knani 2016 states mouse and human results side by side and treats them as concordant (source_calls_it=match, comparison_stated=true), so a literal reading of the `same` rule could apply. I scored untested because (a) the patient source, Motaghedi 2011 (doi:10.1016/j.ejmg.2010.09.015, Eur J Med Genet 54(1):14-8, epub 2010-10-20; abstract only), itself reports only 'a trend for weight loss' in a trial terminated at N=10 after 50% of the rimonabant arm withdrew, with no results ever posted on NCT00603109 (first posted 2008-01-28, stopped for 'Drug side effects'); (b) the mice received JD5037/SLV319, not rimonabant (product_in_model=false); and (c) the model was first used five years after the trial, so it retrodicted a trend rather than predicting a result. Carias & Wevrick 2019 (doi:10.1016/j.omtm.2019.03.001, review, full text read) list JD5037 as the only CB1-system agent tested in a PWS model and note that trials are being run for agents never tested preclinically. The DB's one program, cannabidiol oral solution (Insys, then Radius RAD011), is such a case: NCT02844933 (n=7; HQ-CT median change -4.5 vs -2 on placebo, no analysis; stopped by Insys Chapter 11; results first posted 2023-08-01) and NCT05098509 (n=4, no efficacy analysis, stopped for corporate priorities; results first posted 2023-10-19) had no PWS-model data behind them; the first cannabinoid-family Magel2 study, the CBDA methyl ester EPM301 (Ben-Cnaan 2022, doi:10.3390/ijms23105610, abstract only), came after both trials began and tested a different molecule. No peer-reviewed comparison of any cannabidiol result with a PWS model exists.

safety.note: Peripheral restriction answered rimonabant's psychiatric withdrawals in half the PWS drug arm; the mouse was asked brain exposure (<2%), never behaviour or patients.
safety.short: Mouse asked brain exposure, not psychiatry
safety.quote: However, because of neuropsychiatric side effects such as anxiety, dysthymia, and paranoia and the increased susceptibility to psychiatric disorders, the use of rimonabant is no recommended in PWS.
safety.reason: Psychiatric harm came from patients, not model
safety.judgement: Quote is verbatim including the source's 'no recommended' typo. No PWS model preceded rimonabant; its psychiatric liability in PWS (Motaghedi 2011: 50% of the drug arm withdrew, study terminated) was learned in patients and from the adult-obesity programme. The Magel2 model was then used only to show JD5037 brain/plasma <2% as a surrogate for avoiding that liability; it was never asked a behavioural safety question and JD5037 never reached PWS patients, so there is no model safety prediction to compare. An empty safety list would be the alternative reading. Cannabidiol trial AEs (NCT02844933: no SAEs, diarrhoea/rash in 4/4 treated; NCT05098509: no SAEs in 4) likewise had no model counterpart.
